client.name: Jamie Kelly
client.gradeSummary: The site has a branded keyword #1 ranking and decent direct traffic (11,620 sessions), but catastrophic mobile performance (PageSpeed 30/100, LCP 15.8s, CLS 0.80), a massively bloated sitemap (2,984 URLs of mostly thin IDX filter pages), broken schema markup, and near-zero organic visibility for high-value non-branded keywords. Only 1 of 10 tracked keywords ranks in the top 10. Competitors RE/MAX Mammoth and Resort Realty significantly outperform in both technical SEO and SERP visibility.

topIssues.detail: PageSpeed mobile score of 30/100 with 15.8s LCP, 0.80 CLS, and 16.2s Time to Interactive. 1,027 KiB of unused JavaScript. RE/MAX scores 79/100 on mobile.

topIssues.issue: Massively bloated sitemap with thin IDX pages
topIssues.detail: 2,984 URLs in sitemap, but only ~70 contain unique content. The remaining ~2,900 are auto-generated IDX filter pages (e.g., /bishop-homes-for-sale/2-bedroom/) with thin, duplicative content that dilutes crawl budget.

topIssues.issue: Multiple H1 tags and heading hierarchy issues
topIssues.detail: Homepage has 4 H1 tags ('Find Your Mammoth Lakes Home', 'IMAGINE', 'LIVING HERE', 'Welcome'). Blog page has 5 H1s. About page has 2 H1s (one empty). Property search results page has NO H1.

Organization schema has empty 'name' field. Article schema on blog/about has empty author, publisher.name, and contentLocation. About page uses Article type instead of AboutPage. Community and contact pages have NO schema at all.

topIssues.issue: 93-94% of listing images missing alt text
topIssues.detail: Property search results page: 476 images with 447 missing alt (94%). Full listing page: 1,425 images with 1,339 missing alt (94%). This is a massive accessibility and SEO failure.

topIssues.issue: Wrong-city title tag on property search sitemap
topIssues.detail: The /property-search/site-map/ page displays 'Louisville Area MLS Listings' as its title -- a platform default from the wrong city entirely.

Not ranking at all for 'mammoth lakes homes for sale' (1,600 mo/search), 'mammoth mountain homes for sale' (1,600), 'mammoth lakes condos for sale' (590), 'mammoth lakes vacation homes' (1,300), or 'june lake homes for sale' (590). Only 5 of 10 tracked keywords show any ranking.

competitorStrategies.detail: Mammoth Lakes Resort Realty uses RealEstateAgent schema with full address, geo coordinates, areaServed, sameAs links to social profiles. This enables rich results and knowledge panel potential. Client has generic Organization with empty name field.

Resort Realty runs only 1,246 DOM elements and 23 scripts vs. client's 2,607 elements and 52 scripts, resulting in faster load times and better mobile experience despite both being local real estate sites.

RE/MAX Mammoth ranks in the top 10 for 7 of 10 tracked keywords with avg position 9.2. They achieve this with a simple but fast site (79/100 mobile PageSpeed, near-zero CLS), proper heading structure, and 96% alt text coverage on homepage images.

Competitors create keyword-targeted pages like 'Ski-In/Ski-Out Condos for Sale' and 'Mammoth Mountain Chalet Homes for Sale' that rank for specific search intents. Client relies on generic IDX filter pages that don't target specific buyer interests.
Resort Realty's /market-statistics/ page ranks #11 for 'mammoth lakes real estate' (720/mo search volume). Client has no equivalent data-driven content despite this being a prime content opportunity.

RE/MAX has dedicated pages for June Lake and Crowley Lake real estate that rank #9 and #6 respectively. Client's Crowley Lake page ranks #11 but through a filter page (/open-houses/), not a dedicated landing page.

searchConsoleData.insights: Search Console reveals extremely low organic visibility. Only 6 total clicks across the entire tracking period, with 457 impressions. The homepage averages position 10.47 -- just barely off page 1. Most impressions come from address-specific listing queries, not high-value real estate keywords. The agent page for Jamie Kelly (position 4.0) and the Mammoth Lakes Living page (position 8.92) are bright spots that could be optimized further.

trafficData.insights: The site is heavily dependent on direct traffic (79.1%) and paid search (11.9%). Organic Google search drives only 4.5% of sessions (665) with ZERO conversions from organic. Paid search converts better (7 conversions) but at a cost. Mobile users actually convert better (12 conversions, lower bounce rate 53%) than desktop (0 conversions, 69% bounce rate) despite the catastrophic mobile PageSpeed score. The /mammoth-lakes-homes-for-sale/lake and /on-golf-course filter pages generate the only conversions from landing pages, suggesting buyers landing on specific property-type pages convert better. Notable: ChatGPT already sends traffic (4 sessions, 1 conversion) -- an emerging channel worth optimizing for.
